questions.question: What conventions does Rails use?
questions.title: Rails Conventions
questions.direct_answer: Rails runs on convention over configuration: names line up automatically, so you write little glue. Model: Post is app/models/post.rb, table posts. Controller: PostsController is app/controllers/posts_controller.rb, maps to views in app/views/posts/. Routes: resources :posts gives the 7 actions. Views: app/views/posts/show.html.erb renders by convention from PostsController#show. Tests mirror: test/models/post_test.rb. Pluralization matters: Post -> posts (table), PostsController -> posts (views folder). File names are snake_case (posts_controller.rb) matching CamelCase classes (PostsController). Following convention means Rails finds everything without you configuring it.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the naming alignment (Post model -> posts table -> PostsController -> app/views/posts/) and snake_case-file-matches-CamelCase-class.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Naming a controller PostsController but a folder app/views/post/ (singular breaks the convention), or a table post instead of posts.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Convention over configuration: Post model -> app/models/post.rb -> posts table; PostsController -> app/views/posts/. snake_case files match CamelCase classes; Rails finds everything.

Views: app slash views slash posts slash show dot html dot erb renders by convention from PostsController hash show. Tests mirror: test slash models slash post_test dot rb. Pluralization matters: Post to posts (table), PostsController to posts (views folder). File names are snake_case (posts_controller.rb) matching CamelCase classes (PostsController). sections.title: Names Align
sections.content:
Post model -> posts table -> PostsController -> views/posts. snake_case files match CamelCase classes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[Post: app/models/post.rb] --> T[table: posts]
  M --> C[PostsController: app/controllers/posts_controller.rb]
  C --> V[views: app/views/posts/]
```

sections.title: Rails conventions
sections.content:
```ruby
# Model: class Post -> app/models/post.rb, table `posts` (plural)
class Post < ApplicationRecord; end   # table: posts

# Controller: PostsController -> app/controllers/posts_controller.rb
class PostsController < ApplicationController; end
#   -> views in app/views/posts/ (plural)

# View: rendered by convention from PostsController#show
#   app/views/posts/show.html.erb

# Routes: resources :posts -> the 7 actions (index/show/create/...)
#   config/routes.rb: resources :posts

# Tests mirror:
#   test/models/post_test.rb         (for Post)
#   test/controllers/posts_controller_test.rb  (for PostsController)

# Pluralization: Post -> posts (table); PostsController -> posts (views folder).
# snake_case files match CamelCase classes:
#   posts_controller.rb  -> PostsController
#   admin_user.rb        -> AdminUser
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Naming a controller PostsController but a folder app/views/post (singular breaks it).
A table post instead of posts — Rails infers plural by convention.
Naming a file PostsController.rb (PascalCase) — files are snake_case.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Rails uses convention over configuration: names line up automatically.
snake_case files match CamelCase classes (posts_controller.rb -> PostsController).
resources :posts gives the 7 actions; tests mirror (post_test.rb for Post).

Views: app slash views slash posts slash show dot html dot erb renders by convention from PostsController hash show. Tests mirror: test slash models slash post_test dot rb. Pluralization matters: Post to posts (table), PostsController to posts (views folder). File names are snake_case (posts_controller.rb) matching CamelCase classes (PostsController). Following convention means Rails finds everything without you configuring it. A common mistake is naming a controller PostsController but a folder app slash views slash post, singular, which breaks the convention, and a table post instead of posts.
